# botyard_bot (Resource)

Manages a Botyard bot's desired-state record within the configured organization. Creating the resource persists the bot and triggers provisioner reconciliation best-effort. It manages the bot's core identity (name, description, avatar) and its OpenClaw `config` overrides, and exposes runtime placement and control-plane state as read-only attributes; the bot's skill/tool/credential assignments are managed separately.

See [Getting started](https://docs.botyard.io/docs/getting-started) in the Botyard docs.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A bot's core identity. Creating this persists the bot's desired-state record
# and triggers provisioner reconciliation. The slug is derived from the name and
# is exported as a computed attribute.
resource "botyard_bot" "support" {
  name        = "Support Assistant"
  description = "Answers customer questions in the help center."
}

# A bot with OpenClaw config overrides. `config` is a nested attribute, so it
# uses object syntax (`config = { ... }`). Only the fields you set are applied
# over OpenClaw's defaults; omitted fields keep their server default.
#
# The model a bot runs on is not part of `config`: it is derived from the bot's
# LLM credential links. Set it with `botyard_bot_credential_assignment`
# (`scope = "llm"`, ordered by `ordinal`, with an optional `default_model`).
resource "botyard_bot" "researcher" {
  name        = "Research Assistant"
  description = "Runs deep research tasks."

  config = {
    system_prompt_mode = "botyard"
    thinking_default   = "high"
    reasoning_default  = "stream"

    identity = {
      emoji = "🔬"
      theme = "dark"
    }

    heartbeat = {
      every            = "30m"
      light_context    = true
      isolated_session = true

      active_hours = {
        from_time = "09:00"
        to_time   = "17:00"
        timezone  = "America/New_York"
      }
    }

    compaction = {
      reserve_tokens            = 24000
      truncate_after_compaction = true
    }

    session = {
      write_lock_max_hold_ms = 300000
    }

    # Defer tool schemas behind a search surface instead of inlining them.
    tool_search = {
      mode = "auto"
    }
  }
}

# A bot created from a Bot Pack. The pack is installed when the bot is
# created; removing the `pack` block later uninstalls it and keeps the bot.
# `settings` and `connections` apply at creation only. Connection ids are the
# pack version's `pack_version_connection_id`s, as shown by the API's
# connections preview (`POST /v1/orgs/{org_id}/packs/connections/preview`).
data "botyard_pack_version" "crm" {
  slug = "crm-assistant"
}

resource "botyard_mcp_server" "crm" {
  # ... an org MCP server for the pack's CRM connection
}

resource "botyard_bot" "crm" {
  name = "CRM Assistant"

  pack = {
    pack_version_id = data.botyard_pack_version.crm.pack_version_id

    settings = [
      { path = "tool_search", choice = "custom", custom = { value = jsonencode({ mode = "auto" }) } },
    ]

    connections = [
      # Bind a Terraform-managed server...
      {
        pack_version_connection_id = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001"
        choice                     = "use_server"
        use_server                 = { mcp_server_id = botyard_mcp_server.crm.id }
      },
      # ...connect a new account with Runtime Vault references (not OAuth:
      # connect those in the app first, then use `use_server`)...
      {
        pack_version_connection_id = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002"
        choice                     = "create"
        create = {
          accept_metered = true
          setup = {
            kind            = "credential_form"
            credential_form = { vault_entry_refs = { api_key = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-0000000000aa" } }
          }
        }
      },
      # ...or leave one for later.
      {
        pack_version_connection_id = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000003"
        choice                     = "leave_pending"
      },
    ]
  }
}

# Runtime placement (runtime_class, storage_class, runtime_privilege_mode),
# namespace, and control-plane state are read-only, exported for reference.
output "support_bot_slug" {
  value = botyard_bot.support.slug
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A hosted-native bot.
#
# Native bots run on Botyard's own agent loop instead of OpenClaw, and are
# selected by the hosting pair `hosting_type = "hosted"` + `harness =
# "botyard_native"`. They carry a different config shape, so they use the
# `native_config` block — declaring both `config` and `native_config`, or
# pairing a block with the wrong harness, fails at plan time.
#
# `harness` and `hosting_type` are immutable: changing either forces a new bot.
resource "botyard_bot" "triage" {
  name        = "Triage Agent"
  description = "Triages inbound reports on the native runtime."

  hosting_type = "hosted"
  harness      = "botyard_native"

  # A native bot's instructions (its soul) live in its bot files, not here.
  native_config = {
    tool_search = {
      mode                   = "auto"
      auto_threshold_percent = 40
    }

    # Declared, this block owns all three fields: one you leave out is reset
    # to the platform default.
    tool_images = {
      max_dimension_px = 1568
      default_detail   = "high"
    }
  }
}

# The model a native bot runs on is NOT set on the bot: the platform derives it
# from the bot's LLM credential links, so you set it here and read it back from
# `native_config.model_name`.
resource "botyard_bot_credential_assignment" "triage" {
  bot_slug = botyard_bot.triage.slug

  credentials = [
    {
      credential_id = "cred_anthropic_primary"
      scope         = "llm"
      ordinal       = 0
      default_model = "claude-opus-4-8"
    },
  ]
}

resource "botyard_bot_skill_assignment" "triage" {
  bot_slug = botyard_bot.triage.slug

  skill_ids = [
    "b1a7c0de-0000-4000-8000-000000000001",
  ]
}

# Read-only projections of the platform-owned fields: the model comes from the
# credential assignment above, and the host policy is normalized by the API.
output "triage_model" {
  value = botyard_bot.triage.native_config.model_name
}

output "triage_host_policy" {
  value = botyard_bot.triage.native_config.host_policy_json
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Bot display name (1–255 chars). Immutable — changing it forces replacement, as the API derives the bot's slug from the name at creation and does not support renaming.

### Optional

- `avatar_url` (String) Avatar image URL (a DiceBear data URI or a custom URL). Optional — the API stores no avatar when omitted. Removing it from the config clears the stored value (sends JSON null).
- `config` (Attributes) OpenClaw configuration overrides for the bot, applied via the config endpoint (embedded in the create request and sent to `PATCH /config` on update). Only the fields you set are applied over OpenClaw's defaults; omitted fields keep their server default. This block models the patchable config surface incrementally — `addons` and `bot_type` are not yet modeled. The model a bot runs on is not set here: it is derived from the bot's LLM credential links, managed with `botyard_bot_credential_assignment` (`scope = "llm"`, ordered by `ordinal`, with an optional `default_model`). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--config))
- `description` (String) Short human-facing description / role for the bot (max 500 chars). Display metadata only — not injected into the bot's system prompt. Omit to leave unset.
- `harness` (String) Which agent software this bot runs: `openclaw` (default), `botyard_native`, or `claude_code`. Immutable — changing it forces replacement. Declare `config` for `openclaw` and `native_config` for `botyard_native`. The permitted pairs with `hosting_type` are `(hosted, openclaw)`, `(hosted, botyard_native)` and `(self_hosted, claude_code)`.
- `hosting_type` (String) Who runs this bot's runtime: `hosted` (default) or `self_hosted`. Immutable — changing it forces replacement. Must form a permitted pair with `harness`; the API enforces the allowlist behind `GET /orgs/{org_id}/bots/hosting-options`.
- `native_config` (Attributes) Configuration for a native (`botyard_native`) bot, applied via the config endpoint (embedded in the create request and sent to `PATCH /config` on update). Requires `harness = "botyard_native"`, and conflicts with `config`, which models the OpenClaw shape. Only the fields you set are applied over the platform's defaults. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--native_config))
- `pack` (Attributes) A Bot Pack to create this bot from. When set, the bot is created with `POST /bots/from-pack`, which installs the pack in the same transaction. Removing the block uninstalls the pack and keeps the bot. Adding it to an existing bot, or changing `pack_version_id`, is refused at plan time: the API has no install-on-existing-bot or upgrade path yet, and the provider never replaces a bot (that would lose its conversations and memory). `avatar_url` left unset means the pack's avatar is kept. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--pack))

### Read-Only

- `access` (String) Bot visibility within its organization (`open` or `restricted`).
- `config_generation` (Number) Monotonic config generation counter.
- `created_at` (String) Creation timestamp (RFC 3339).
- `desired_state` (String) Control-plane desired lifecycle state.
- `durable_root_owns_home` (Boolean) Operator rollout flag for the single-block durable root layout. When true, `/home/openclaw` lives inside the durable root overlay.
- `health_status` (String) Bot health monitoring status.
- `id` (String) Unique bot identifier (UUID).
- `namespace` (String) Kubernetes namespace for the bot runtime.
- `onboarding_state` (String) Guided-setup lifecycle state of the bot.
- `org_id` (String) Organization ID that owns the bot.
- `runtime_class` (String) Container runtime class for the bot pod (e.g. `kata_qemu`, `runc`, or a cluster default). Set by the platform; not user-configurable.
- `runtime_privilege_mode` (String) Privilege level of the bot runtime pod. Read-only in this provider version.
- `slug` (String) URL-friendly bot identifier, derived from the name at creation. Used as the import ID.
- `storage_class` (String) Storage class for the bot's workspace PVC. Set by the platform; not user-configurable.
- `updated_at` (String) Last-update timestamp (RFC 3339).

<a id="nestedatt--config"></a>
### Nested Schema for `config`

Optional:

- `compaction` (Attributes) Context-compaction safeguards. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--config--compaction))
- `heartbeat` (Attributes) Heartbeat scheduling and behavior. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--config--heartbeat))
- `identity` (Attributes) Bot identity overrides. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--config--identity))
- `reasoning_default` (String) Default reasoning mode: `off`, `on`, or `stream`.
- `session` (Attributes) Session-reliability settings. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--config--session))
- `system_prompt_mode` (String) System prompt source: `botyard` (lean, default) or `openclaw`.
- `thinking_default` (String) Default thinking budget: one of `off`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `adaptive`.
- `tool_search` (Attributes) Tool Search: defer tool schemas out of the prompt behind a search surface instead of inlining every schema on every turn. Removing this block does NOT reset the setting: the API's target field is non-nullable with a default, so a patch that omits it means "no change" and the last applied values persist. Set the fields explicitly to change them. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--config--tool_search))

<a id="nestedatt--config--compaction"></a>
### Nested Schema for `config.compaction`

Optional:

- `max_active_transcript_bytes` (Number) Byte size that triggers proactive local compaction.
- `mid_turn_precheck` (Boolean) Run a tool-loop context precheck before the next model call.
- `reserve_tokens` (Number) Reply/tool headroom tokens reserved after compaction.
- `reserve_tokens_floor` (Number) Floor enforced for `reserve_tokens` (0 disables).
- `timeout_seconds` (Number) Maximum seconds allowed for one compaction operation.
- `truncate_after_compaction` (Boolean) Rotate the active transcript to a compacted successor.


<a id="nestedatt--config--heartbeat"></a>
### Nested Schema for `config.heartbeat`

Optional:

- `ack_max_chars` (Number) Max characters after `HEARTBEAT_OK` before delivery.
- `active_hours` (Attributes) Time window when heartbeats are active. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--config--heartbeat--active_hours))
- `every` (String) Heartbeat interval: one of `0m` (disabled), `5m`, `15m`, `30m`, `1h`, `2h`, `6h`, `12h`, `24h`, `168h`.
- `include_reasoning` (Boolean) Include reasoning traces in heartbeat responses.
- `isolated_session` (Boolean) Run each heartbeat in a fresh session with no history.
- `light_context` (Boolean) Use minimal context (only HEARTBEAT.md) to reduce token cost.
- `model` (String) LLM model override for heartbeat runs.
- `prompt` (String) Custom prompt replacing the default HEARTBEAT.md reader.

<a id="nestedatt--config--heartbeat--active_hours"></a>
### Nested Schema for `config.heartbeat.active_hours`

Required:

- `from_time` (String) Start time in `HH:MM` format (e.g. `09:00`).
- `timezone` (String) IANA timezone (e.g. `America/New_York`).
- `to_time` (String) End time in `HH:MM` format (e.g. `17:00`).



<a id="nestedatt--config--identity"></a>
### Nested Schema for `config.identity`

Optional:

- `emoji` (String) Bot identity emoji.
- `theme` (String) Bot identity theme.


<a id="nestedatt--config--session"></a>
### Nested Schema for `config.session`

Optional:

- `write_lock_max_hold_ms` (Number) Watchdog force-release threshold for the session write-lock (ms).


<a id="nestedatt--config--tool_search"></a>
### Nested Schema for `config.tool_search`

Optional:

- `auto_threshold_percent` (Number) Percentage (0 to 100) of the context window the tool schemas must exceed before `auto` defers them. Ignored unless `mode` is `auto`, and read only by the Claude Code runtime; OpenClaw's embedded Tool Search has no threshold, so `auto` behaves like `always` there.
- `mode` (String) `always` (defer every turn), `auto` (defer above the threshold), or `off` (never defer). The platform default is `auto`.



<a id="nestedatt--native_config"></a>
### Nested Schema for `native_config`

Optional:

- `tool_images` (Attributes) How images returned by the bot's tools are shown to the model. Once this block is declared it owns all three fields: a field you leave out is sent as null, which resets it to the platform default. Removing the whole block leaves the last applied values in place, because the API treats an omitted `tool_images` as "no change". To return to the defaults, apply an empty block, `tool_images = {}`, first. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--native_config--tool_images))
- `tool_search` (Attributes) Tool Search: defer tool schemas out of the prompt behind a search surface instead of inlining every schema on every turn. Removing this block does NOT reset the setting: the API's target field is non-nullable with a default, so a patch that omits it means "no change" and the last applied values persist. Set the fields explicitly to change them. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--native_config--tool_search))

Read-Only:

- `host_policy_json` (String) The bot's operator host policy, as JSON. **Read-only** — the platform owns this value and normalizes it, and an invalid policy is a fatal runtime startup failure, so it is not writable from Terraform.
- `model_name` (String) Model the broker routes this bot to. **Read-only** — derived from the bot's LLM credential links (chain position 0), not from this resource.
- `model_provider` (String) Provider of the model the broker routes this bot to. **Read-only** — the platform derives it from the bot's LLM credential links; manage it with `botyard_bot_credential_assignment`.

<a id="nestedatt--native_config--tool_images"></a>
### Nested Schema for `native_config.tool_images`

Optional:

- `default_detail` (String) Detail level for a tool image whose MCP server does not request one: `auto`, `low`, `high` or `original`. Unset leaves it to the model provider's default.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Show images returned by tools to the model. `false` replaces each image with a short text notice. Unset means enabled.
- `max_dimension_px` (Number) Longest edge, in pixels, a tool image is downscaled to before the model sees it, from 1 to 8000. Unset means the platform default (2000). Values above 2000 only take effect while a request holds 20 images or fewer.


<a id="nestedatt--native_config--tool_search"></a>
### Nested Schema for `native_config.tool_search`

Optional:

- `auto_threshold_percent` (Number) Percentage (0 to 100) of the context window the tool schemas must exceed before `auto` defers them. Ignored unless `mode` is `auto`, and read only by the Claude Code runtime; OpenClaw's embedded Tool Search has no threshold, so `auto` behaves like `always` there.
- `mode` (String) `always` (defer every turn), `auto` (defer above the threshold), or `off` (never defer). The platform default is `auto`.



<a id="nestedatt--pack"></a>
### Nested Schema for `pack`

Required:

- `pack_version_id` (String) The pack version to install, e.g. `data.botyard_pack.support.latest.pack_version_id`. Changing it is a plan-time error until the API offers in-place upgrades.

Optional:

- `connections` (Attributes List) Per MCP connection of the pack version: `use_server` binds an org MCP server, `leave_pending` binds nothing, and `create` connects a new account with Runtime Vault references. A connection left out binds the one visible server from its catalogue entry, as in the app. Applied at creation only. A connection that needs a vendor sign-in (OAuth) cannot be created here: connect it in the app first, then use `use_server` or `leave_pending`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--pack--connections))
- `settings` (Attributes List) Per pack setting: `pack` (the default for a setting left out), `keep` the bot's own value, or `custom` with a `custom = { value }` payload. Applied at creation only. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--pack--settings))

Read-Only:

- `bot_pack_install_id` (String) The install's id.
- `pack_id` (String) The installed pack's id.
- `pack_slug` (String) The installed pack's slug.
- `pending_connections` (Attributes List) Connections whose setup is not done, in connection order. Finish them in the app; they refresh on every read. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--pack--pending_connections))
- `version_no` (Number) The installed version's number.

<a id="nestedatt--pack--connections"></a>
### Nested Schema for `pack.connections`

Required:

- `choice` (String) `use_server`, `leave_pending` or `create`.
- `pack_version_connection_id` (String) A connection of the pack version.

Optional:

- `create` (Attributes) `choice = "create"` only, and required for it: the new account. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--pack--connections--create))
- `use_server` (Attributes) `choice = "use_server"` only, and required for it. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--pack--connections--use_server))

<a id="nestedatt--pack--connections--create"></a>
### Nested Schema for `pack.connections.create`

Required:

- `setup` (Attributes) What the new account needs, matching the connection's setup kind. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--pack--connections--create--setup))

Optional:

- `accept_metered` (Boolean) Must be `true` when the connection is metered: the new server is billed as a hosted MCP server.
- `name` (String) The new server's name. Defaults to the catalogue entry's.

<a id="nestedatt--pack--connections--create--setup"></a>
### Nested Schema for `pack.connections.create.setup`

Required:

- `kind` (String) `none`, `setup_form` or `credential_form`.

Optional:

- `credential_form` (Attributes) `kind = "credential_form"` only, and required for it. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--pack--connections--create--setup--credential_form))
- `setup_form` (Attributes) `kind = "setup_form"` only, and required for it. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--pack--connections--create--setup--setup_form))

<a id="nestedatt--pack--connections--create--setup--credential_form"></a>
### Nested Schema for `pack.connections.create.setup.credential_form`

Required:

- `vault_entry_refs` (Map of String) Credential field name to the id of an org Runtime Vault secret holding its value. At least one.


<a id="nestedatt--pack--connections--create--setup--setup_form"></a>
### Nested Schema for `pack.connections.create.setup.setup_form`

Required:

- `catalog_form_answers` (Attributes Map) Field id to answer. A secret field must be `mode = "secret_ref"` with a Runtime Vault key path. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--pack--connections--create--setup--setup_form--catalog_form_answers))

<a id="nestedatt--pack--connections--create--setup--setup_form--catalog_form_answers"></a>
### Nested Schema for `pack.connections.create.setup.setup_form.catalog_form_answers`

Required:

- `mode` (String) `plaintext` or `secret_ref`.
- `value` (String) The plaintext value, or the vault key path for `secret_ref`.





<a id="nestedatt--pack--connections--use_server"></a>
### Nested Schema for `pack.connections.use_server`

Required:

- `mcp_server_id` (String) The org MCP server to bind, e.g. `botyard_mcp_server.crm.id`.



<a id="nestedatt--pack--settings"></a>
### Nested Schema for `pack.settings`

Required:

- `choice` (String) `pack`, `keep` or `custom`.
- `path` (String) The pack setting, e.g. `tool_search`.

Optional:

- `custom` (Attributes) `choice = "custom"` only, and required for it. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--pack--settings--custom))

<a id="nestedatt--pack--settings--custom"></a>
### Nested Schema for `pack.settings.custom`

Required:

- `value` (String) The value as JSON, in the setting's own shape, e.g. `jsonencode({ mode = "auto" })` for `tool_search`.



<a id="nestedatt--pack--pending_connections"></a>
### Nested Schema for `pack.pending_connections`

Read-Only:

- `bot_pack_connection_setup_id` (String) Its setup.
- `pack_version_connection_id` (String) The connection.
- `state` (String) Where the setup is, e.g. `needs_input`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Bots are imported by their slug (the API's URL identifier).
terraform import botyard_bot.support support-assistant

# A bot with a Bot Pack install: `<slug>` alone adopts the install only when the
# bot has exactly one (none imports no `pack` block). With several installs it
# is an error that lists them; name the one this resource manages instead, by
# install id or, when that pack slug is installed once on the bot, by pack slug:
terraform import botyard_bot.support support-assistant:0b6c1f9e-4f7a-4d2b-9a51-3c2e8d7f6a10
terraform import botyard_bot.support support-assistant:crm-assistant
# `pack.settings` and `pack.connections` are create-time inputs the API cannot
# read back, so they are not imported.
```
